topic_name: Machine Learning I: Overview and Naïve Bayes

topics.title: Machine Learning
topics.overview: Introduction to machine learning concepts, learning from data, parameters, and structures.
topics.summary: Machine learning involves acquiring models from data, learning parameters, structures, and hidden concepts.

topics.title: Supervised Learning
topics.overview: Learning from labeled examples through classification and regression.
topics.summary: Supervised learning uses labeled data to discover functions for classification and regression.

topics.title: Statistical Learning
topics.overview: Learning as a form of probabilistic inference, Bayesian learning, MAP, ML.
topics.summary: Statistical learning involves probabilistic inference using Bayes’ theorem, maximum a posteriori (MAP), and maximum likelihood (ML).

topics.title: Naïve Bayes Classification
topics.overview: A simplistic probabilistic model assuming feature independence.
topics.summary: Naïve Bayes is a classification algorithm that assumes conditional independence of features given a class.

topics.title: Training and Testing
topics.overview: Data splitting into training, validation, and test sets; avoiding overfitting.
topics.summary: Model evaluation involves training, validation, and testing, ensuring generalization and avoiding overfitting.

concept_questions.question: What is supervised learning?
concept_questions.answer: Supervised learning is a machine learning paradigm where models are trained using labeled data to learn a function that maps inputs to outputs.

concept_questions.question: How does Bayesian learning work?
concept_questions.answer: Bayesian learning updates prior probabilities of hypotheses using observed data based on Bayes' theorem.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What assumption does the Naïve Bayes classifier make?
options: A) Features are dependent given the class
B) Features are independent given the class
C) The prior probabilities are equal for all classes
D) It does not use probability distributions
multiple_choice_questions.correct_answer: B) Features are independent given the class

multiple_choice_questions.question: What is overfitting?
options: A) When a model performs well on unseen data
B) When a model captures noise instead of the underlying pattern
C) When a model has too few parameters
D) When a model generalizes well to new data
multiple_choice_questions.correct_answer: B) When a model captures noise instead of the underlying pattern
